reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis incorrectly assumes that lattice distortion in BCC refractory high-entropy alloys lowers stacking fault energy and promotes twinning, whereas BCC metals generally have high stacking fault energies and deform by screw dislocation motion, not twinning, at high temperatures.
reasons.testability: The proposed in situ TEM tensile test at 1000–1200 °C is extremely challenging and the falsification criteria (e.g., quantifying mobile dislocation density and twin formation) are not clearly defined or practical for BCC alloys at these temperatures.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it is based on a fundamental misunderstanding of deformation mechanisms in BCC refractory alloys, leading researchers down an unproductive path.
